title: Privacy policy
body_html:
This policy explains what personal information we collect when you shop with Raqello, how we use it and the choices you have. We have kept it short and in plain English.

Who we are

Raqello is run by [Company name] Ltd, a company registered under company number [company number]. Our registered address is [registered address].

We are the controller of the personal information described in this policy. This means we decide how and why it is used, and we are responsible for looking after it under the UK General Data Protection Regulation (UK GDPR) and the Data Protection Act 2018.

If you have any questions about this policy or your information, email us at hello@raqello.com.

What we collect

When you place an order, we collect your name, email address, phone number, delivery address and billing address. We also keep details of what you bought and how you paid.

If you create an account, we keep your login details and your order history. If you contact us, we keep a record of the conversation and anything you send us, such as photos of a faulty item.

When you browse our website, we collect technical information such as your IP address, device, browser and the pages you visit. Some of this comes from cookies, which are explained in our cookie policy.

We do not see or store your full card details. Payments are handled securely by our payment providers.

Information from other sources

Some information comes to us from the companies we work with. Our payment providers, including PayPal and Klarna, tell us whether a payment has been approved and may flag an order that looks fraudulent.

Our delivery couriers tell us when a parcel has been delivered or if there was a problem. If you leave a review on Trustpilot, Trustpilot shares it with us so we can read it and reply.

How we use your information and our lawful bases

We only use your personal information when the law allows it. Most often, we use it to carry out our contract with you. This covers processing your order, taking payment, arranging delivery, handling returns and refunds, and running your account.

We also use it to meet our legal obligations. For example, we keep records of orders and payments because tax and accounting law requires us to, and we share information with authorities when the law says we must.

Some uses are in our legitimate interests, as long as these are not outweighed by your rights. These include preventing fraud, keeping our website secure, answering your questions, sending you messages about your orders, improving our website using analytics and inviting you to review your purchase on Trustpilot. You can object to any of these.

We rely on your consent to send you our newsletter and to set cookies that are not strictly necessary. You can withdraw your consent at any time.

Newsletters and how to unsubscribe

We only send you our newsletter if you have signed up for it. It gives you news about our products and our store.

We send our newsletter through our email platform. It stores your email address and records whether you open our emails and click the links in them. This helps us understand what is useful to you.

You can unsubscribe at any time by clicking the unsubscribe link at the bottom of any newsletter, or by emailing hello@raqello.com. Unsubscribing does not stop emails about your orders, such as order and dispatch confirmations.

After you unsubscribe, we keep your email address on a list of people who do not want marketing. This makes sure we do not email you again by mistake.

Who we share your information with

We only share your information with organisations that help us run our store, and only what they need. We never sell your personal information.

Shopify hosts our website and checkout and stores our order and customer records. Our payment providers process your payment, including PayPal if you pay with PayPal and Klarna if you choose Klarna. PayPal and Klarna also use your information for their own purposes, such as fraud checks and, for Klarna, deciding whether to offer you credit. Their own privacy notices explain how.

Our delivery couriers receive your name, address, email address and phone number so they can deliver your order and send you updates. Trustpilot receives your name, email address and order reference so it can invite you to leave a review. Our email platform holds your details if you sign up for our newsletter. Our analytics provider helps us understand how people use our website.

We may also share information with our professional advisers, with the police, HMRC or other authorities where the law requires it, or with a buyer if our business is sold. Where a provider handles information for us, our contract with them requires them to keep it secure and only use it as we instruct.

International transfers

Some of our providers, including Shopify, PayPal, Klarna, Trustpilot and our email platform and analytics provider, may store or access your information outside the UK. This can include the European Economic Area, Canada and the United States.

When your information is transferred outside the UK, we make sure it is protected. Either the country has been approved by the UK government as having adequate data protection laws, or the transfer is covered by safeguards recognised under UK law, such as the International Data Transfer Agreement or the UK Addendum to the EU standard contractual clauses.

Contact us if you would like more information about these safeguards.

How long we keep your information

We only keep your information for as long as we need it for the purposes in this policy.

We keep order, payment and refund records for as long as tax and accounting law requires, which is usually six years.

We keep your account details while your account is open. If you ask us to close it, we delete your account details but keep your order records for the period above. We keep messages with our customer team for as long as we need them to deal with your query and any follow up.

If you sign up for our newsletter, we keep your details until you unsubscribe. Cookies are kept for the periods explained in our cookie policy.

Keeping your information safe

Our website and checkout run on Shopify and use encrypted connections. Only people who need customer information to do their job can access it.

No website can be completely secure, so please keep your account password private. Tell us straight away if you think someone else has used your account.

Your rights

You have rights over your personal information. You can ask for a copy of the information we hold about you, ask us to correct anything that is wrong or incomplete, and ask us to delete your information.

You can also ask us to limit how we use your information, object to us using it for our legitimate interests, and ask us to send information you gave us to you or another organisation in a commonly used format. You can object to direct marketing at any time, and we will stop.

Where we rely on your consent, you can withdraw it at any time. This does not affect anything we did before you withdrew it.

To use any of these rights, email hello@raqello.com. We may need to check your identity first. We will reply within one month and will not normally charge you. Some rights do not apply in every situation. For example, we must keep order records that the law requires us to keep. We will explain if this is the case.

How to complain

If you are unhappy with how we have handled your information, please contact us first at hello@raqello.com so we can try to put things right.

You also have the right to complain to the Information Commissioner's Office (ICO), the UK regulator for data protection. You can contact the ICO through its website at ico.org.uk or by calling its helpline on 0303 123 1113.

Contacting us

For any question about this policy or your personal information, email hello@raqello.com. Our customer team is available Monday to Friday, 9am to 5pm.

You can also write to us at [Company name] Ltd, [registered address].

Changes to this policy

We may update this policy from time to time, for example if we change how we use your information or if the law changes. The latest version will always be on this page.

If we make a significant change that affects you, we will tell you on our website or by email.

title: Terms and conditions
body_html:
These terms apply when you use our website and buy from Raqello. Please read them before you place an order. They do not affect your legal rights as a consumer.

Who we are

This website is run by [Company name] Ltd, a company registered under company number [company number]. Our registered address is [registered address] and our VAT number is [VAT number].

In these terms, "we", "us" and "our" mean [Company name] Ltd. "You" means the person using our website or buying from us.

You can contact us by email at hello@raqello.com. Our customer team is available Monday to Friday, 9am to 5pm.

Using our website and your account

You may use our website to browse and buy products for your own use. Please do not misuse it, for example by trying to gain unauthorised access or introducing viruses.

All text, images and designs on our website belong to us or the people we license them from. You must not copy or reuse them without our permission.

We try to keep our website running smoothly, but we cannot promise it will always be available or free from errors. Links to other websites are for your information only, and we are not responsible for their content.

If you create an account, please keep your login details private and tell us straight away if you think someone else has used it. You can ask us to close your account at any time by emailing hello@raqello.com. We may suspend or close an account that is being used fraudulently or in breach of these terms.

Orders and when a contract is made

When you place an order, we will email you to confirm we have received it. This email does not mean we have accepted your order.

A contract between you and us is made when we email you to confirm your order has been dispatched. Only the items listed in that email are part of the contract.

Sometimes we may not be able to accept your order. For example, an item may be out of stock, there may be an error in the price or description, we may not be able to deliver to your address, or your payment may not be authorised. If this happens, we will tell you and refund any payment you have made in full.

Please check your order carefully before you submit it, especially sizes and your delivery address. If you spot a mistake, contact us as soon as possible and we will try to help before your order is dispatched.

Prices and payment

All prices are in pounds sterling and include VAT. Any delivery charge is shown at checkout before you pay.

We work hard to make sure our prices are correct. If we find an error in the price of an item you have ordered, we will contact you. You can then choose to go ahead at the correct price or cancel your order for a full refund.

You can pay by debit or credit card, PayPal, Apple Pay or Klarna. We take payment when you place your order. If you pay with PayPal, PayPal's own terms also apply.

If you choose Klarna Pay in 3, you split the cost into three payments. Pay in 3 is a credit agreement between you and Klarna, not with us. Klarna decides whether to offer it to you and shows you its terms, including what happens if you miss a payment, before you confirm. Paying late could affect your ability to use Klarna and to borrow in future.

Delivery

We deliver to addresses in the UK only. Standard delivery usually takes 3 to 5 working days. Delivery to the Highlands, Islands and Northern Ireland usually takes 4 to 7 working days.

Standard delivery is free on orders over £75. On all other orders it costs £4.95.

Delivery times are estimates. If we expect a delay, we will let you know. If we do not deliver within 30 days of the contract being made, or by a date we agreed with you, you may have the right to end the contract and get a full refund.

Your order is your responsibility once it has been delivered to the address you gave us. It becomes your property once we have received full payment. If a parcel arrives damaged or an item is missing, please contact us as soon as you can.

Your right to cancel and our 14 day returns

Under the Consumer Contracts (Information, Cancellation and Additional Charges) Regulations 2013, you can cancel your order for any reason within 14 days. The 14 days start on the day after you receive your order. If your order arrives in more than one delivery, they start on the day after the last item arrives.

To cancel, start a return on our website or email us at hello@raqello.com within that time. You then have a further 14 days to send the items back. Our 14 day returns policy works alongside this right. Items should be unused and in their original packaging.

You can handle an item as you would in a shop to check it. If an item has been used or damaged, we may reduce your refund to reflect the loss in value. If you have changed your mind, you pay the cost of sending items back, so we recommend a tracked service.

We refund you within 5 working days of your return arriving with us, to the payment method you used. If you cancel your whole order, we also refund the standard delivery charge you paid. If you paid with Klarna, Klarna updates your payment plan and refunds anything you have already paid.

Faulty goods and your legal rights

Under the Consumer Rights Act 2015, the goods we sell must be of satisfactory quality, fit for purpose and as described. Nothing in these terms affects these rights.

If an item is faulty, you can reject it and get a full refund within 30 days of receiving it. After 30 days, you can ask for a repair or a replacement. If that is not possible or does not fix the problem, you can ask for a refund or a price reduction.

If a fault appears within six months of delivery, it is assumed to have been there when the item was delivered, unless we can show otherwise. After six months, you may need to show that the fault was there at delivery. You can make a claim for up to six years after delivery, or five years in Scotland.

Normal wear and tear, accidental damage and damage caused by misuse are not faults. To report a fault, email hello@raqello.com with your order number and photos if you can. If an item is faulty or we sent you the wrong item, we cover the cost of returning it.

Manufacturer warranties

Some brands offer their own warranty on their products. Where a brand offers one, it is provided by the brand, and claims are handled through the brand under its own terms.

A manufacturer warranty is in addition to your legal rights under the Consumer Rights Act 2015 and does not replace them. If an item is faulty, you can still come to us. If you are not sure where to start, contact our customer team and we will point you in the right direction.

Product information and images

We try to make sure our product descriptions, specifications and images are accurate. Much of the technical information comes from the brands we sell.

Colours can look different on different screens, and images are for illustration. Brands sometimes update designs or packaging, so the item you receive may look slightly different from the photo. This does not affect your rights if an item is not as described.

Any guides or advice on our website are general information to help you choose. They are not a promise that a product will suit you.

Our liability to you

If we break these terms, we are responsible for loss or damage you suffer that is a foreseeable result of our breach or our failure to use reasonable care. Loss is foreseeable if it is obvious it will happen, or if we both knew it might happen when the contract was made. We are not responsible for loss that is not foreseeable.

We do not exclude or limit our liability where it would be unlawful to do so. This includes liability for death or personal injury caused by our negligence, for fraud, and for breaking your legal rights in relation to the products we sell.

We sell products for domestic and private use. We are not liable to you for any loss of profit, loss of business or business interruption.

Events outside our control

We are not responsible for delays or failures caused by events outside our reasonable control. These include severe weather, strikes, disruption to courier services and failures of systems we rely on.

If this happens, we will contact you as soon as we can and do what we can to reduce the delay. If there is a risk of a substantial delay, you can contact us to cancel your order. We will refund you for any products you have paid for but not received.

Governing law

These terms are governed by the law of England and Wales. You can bring legal proceedings in the courts of England and Wales. If you live in Scotland, you can also bring proceedings in Scotland. If you live in Northern Ireland, you can also bring proceedings in Northern Ireland.

If you have a problem with your order, please contact us first. We will always try to put things right with you directly.

If a court decides that any part of these terms is invalid, the rest of the terms will still apply.

Changes to these terms

We may update these terms from time to time, for example to reflect changes in the law or in how we run our store.

The terms that apply to your order are the ones shown on our website when you placed it. Please check this page each time you order.

Contact us

If you have any questions about these terms or your order, email us at hello@raqello.com. Our customer team is available Monday to Friday, 9am to 5pm.

You can also write to us at [Company name] Ltd, [registered address]. Please include your order number if you have one.

title: Cookie policy
body_html:
This policy explains how Raqello uses cookies and similar technologies on our website, and how you can choose which ones we use.

What cookies are

Cookies are small text files that a website saves on your computer, phone or tablet when you visit. They let the website remember things, such as what is in your bag, from one page to the next and between visits.

Some cookies are set by us. Others are set by third parties whose services we use on our website. Some cookies last only until you close your browser. Others stay on your device for a set period or until you delete them.

We also use similar technologies, such as pixels and local storage, which work in much the same way. In this policy, we use the word cookies to cover all of them.

Cookies and the law

The use of cookies in the UK is covered by the Privacy and Electronic Communications Regulations 2003 (PECR). Under PECR, we must tell you which cookies we use and why. We must also ask for your consent before setting cookies that are not strictly necessary.

When you first visit our website, we ask you to choose which types of cookie you are happy for us to use. We only set preference, analytics and marketing cookies if you agree.

Where cookies collect personal information, our privacy policy also applies.

Strictly necessary cookies

These cookies are needed for our website to work. They keep track of what is in your bag, take you securely through checkout, keep you signed in to your account and remember your cookie choices.

They also help protect our website and our customers, for example by preventing fraud. Because the website cannot work properly without them, these cookies do not need your consent and cannot be switched off in our cookie settings.

Most strictly necessary cookies on our website are set by Shopify, which runs our store and checkout. PayPal and Klarna may also set them when you pay.

Preference cookies

Preference cookies remember choices you make on our website, so it works the way you expect when you come back.

We only set preference cookies if you agree. If you turn them off, the website will still work, but it may not remember your choices.

Analytics cookies

Analytics cookies help us understand how people use our website. They tell us things like which pages are visited most, how people find us and where they run into problems.

We use this information to improve our website and make it easier to shop. We look at it in a combined form and do not use it to identify you.

Analytics cookies are set by Shopify and by our analytics provider. We only set them if you agree.

Marketing cookies

Marketing cookies help us understand whether our newsletters and any advertising bring people to our website and lead to orders. They can also be used to show you adverts on other websites that are more relevant to you.

These cookies may be set by us or by third parties, and they can recognise your browser across different websites. We only set them if you agree. If you turn them off, you may still see adverts, but they will be less relevant to you.

Third party cookies

Some cookies on our website are set by the companies whose services we use. Shopify runs our website and checkout. It sets cookies for your bag, checkout, security and its own analytics.

Klarna may set cookies when you view Klarna information on our website or choose Klarna at checkout, including to help prevent fraud. PayPal may set cookies when you choose to pay with PayPal, including to keep your payment secure.

Trustpilot may set cookies when our website shows Trustpilot reviews or ratings. Our analytics provider sets cookies to measure how our website is used, if you agree.

We do not control these cookies. Each company explains how it uses cookies and personal information in its own cookie and privacy policies, which you can find on its website.

Managing your cookie choices

You can change your cookie choices at any time. Use the Cookie settings link at the bottom of any page on our website to turn preference, analytics and marketing cookies on or off.

If you withdraw your consent, we will stop setting those cookies from then on. This does not affect anything that happened before you changed your choice. To remove cookies that are already on your device, delete them in your browser settings.

Using your browser settings

Most browsers let you see which cookies are stored, delete them and block them, either for all websites or for particular ones. You can usually find these options in your browser settings or help pages.

If you block all cookies, including strictly necessary ones, parts of our website will not work. You may not be able to add items to your bag or complete checkout.

Your cookie choices are saved on the device and browser you use. If you use a different device or browser, or clear your cookies, you will need to choose again.

Changes to this policy

We may update this policy if we change the cookies we use or if the law changes. The latest version will always be on this page.

If we make a significant change, we may ask you for your cookie choices again.

Contact us

If you have any questions about how we use cookies, email us at hello@raqello.com. Our customer team is available Monday to Friday, 9am to 5pm.

You can also write to us at [Company name] Ltd, [registered address]. To find out more about how we handle your personal information, please read our privacy policy.
